subject: cs
input: What retrieval strategies improve citation faithfulness in scientific question answering?
output: Dense bi-encoder retrieval followed by cross-encoder reranking improves citation faithfulness because the reranker promotes passages that directly support each claim. Combining lexical BM25 signals with dense retrieval (hybrid retrieval) further raises recall of supporting evidence. Attribution is then verified by checking that each cited passage entails the corresponding answer sentence.

ctxs.text: Combining lexical BM25 signals with dense retrieval raises recall of supporting evidence over either method alone on scientific corpora.

ctxs.title: Attribution evaluation via entailment
ctxs.text: Attribution is verified by checking that each cited passage entails the corresponding answer sentence using a natural language inference model.

subject: cs
input: How do language models reduce hallucination when answering from a corpus?
output: Retrieval-augmented generation reduces hallucination by grounding each generated claim in retrieved documents. Constraining the model to cite only retrieved passages and dropping citations whose supporting quote is not verbatim present further limits fabricated references.

ctxs.title: Retrieval-augmented generation grounding

subject: bio
input: What single-cell methods characterise the tumour microenvironment?
output: Single-cell RNA sequencing resolves the cellular composition of the tumour microenvironment, distinguishing malignant cells from immune and stromal populations. Spatial transcriptomics adds tissue context by mapping expression to location, revealing how immune infiltration varies across the tumour.

ctxs.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing of tumours
ctxs.text: Single-cell RNA sequencing resolves the cellular composition of the tumour microenvironment, distinguishing malignant cells from immune and stromal populations.

ctxs.title: Spatial transcriptomics of solid tumours
ctxs.text: Spatial transcriptomics adds tissue context by mapping expression to location, revealing how immune infiltration varies across the tumour.

ctxs.title: Bulk RNA sequencing limitations
ctxs.text: Bulk RNA sequencing averages expression across all cells and cannot resolve rare immune subpopulations within a tumour.

subject: bio
input: How are protein structures predicted from sequence?
output: Deep learning models predict protein three-dimensional structure directly from amino acid sequence using evolutionary couplings inferred from multiple sequence alignments. Attention-based architectures model long-range residue interactions, achieving near-experimental accuracy on many targets.

ctxs.title: Wet-lab crystallography
ctxs.text: X-ray crystallography determines structures experimentally but is slow and does not scale to every protein.

subject: physics
input: How is machine learning used to classify phases of matter?
output: Supervised neural networks classify phases of matter from configurations sampled by Monte Carlo simulation, learning order parameters without explicit feature engineering. Unsupervised methods detect phase transitions by identifying changes in the structure of the configuration distribution.

ctxs.title: Unsupervised detection of transitions
